 Dean Wade (ankle) has been ruled out against the Knicks on Tuesday.
 Wade has been managing an ankle injury that will keep him out of the lineup for the season opener. Justin Edwards and Jabari Walker may be tasked with playing extra minutes off the bench, but neither will play a significant role.

 Dean Wade (ankle) is questionable for Thursday’s game against the Cavaliers. 
 Wade went through an individual workout ahead of Tuesday’s win over the Knicks but was deemed unfit to play. If he can play against his former team on Thursday, that would likely drop Jabari Walker out of the rotation entirely, with Kentavious Caldwell-Pope likely playing less after logging 26 minutes in the opener. 
 Dean Wade 
 PHI 
 Forward-Center 
 #45 
 Dean Wade (ankle) is questionable for Tuesday’s game against the Knicks. 
 Wade was limited to individual work in Monday’s practice, but he could play in Tuesday’s season opener. If he plays, Jabari Walker may get fewer minutes. However, with Adem Bona (foot) also questionable, Walker may play rotation minutes at center instead of power forward. 
 Adem Bona 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #30 
 Adem Bona (foot) is questionable for Tuesday’s game against the Knicks. 
 Bona missed the entire preseason with a sprained left foot, but he could be available for Tuesday’s season opener. While his availability doesn’t affect fantasy basketball, it will factor into how the 76ers handle the back end of their rotation. Jabari Walker may be asked to play some minutes at center, especially with Dominick Barlow and Ariel Hukportin unavailable. 
 Dean Wade 
 PHI 
 Forward-Center 
 #45 
 Dean Wade (ankle) was limited to individual work during Monday’s practice. 
 After spraining his left ankle in Friday’s preseason finale against the Celtics, Wade did not practice on Sunday. He missed team segments of practice on Monday, but the 76ers forward did some individual work. If Wade can’t play, Jabari Walker may get rotation minutes off the bench in Tuesday’s opener against the Knicks. 
 Dean Wade 
 PHI 
 Forward-Center 
 #45 
 Dean Wade (ankle) and Dominick Barlow (back) did not participate in Sunday’s practice. 
 Wade rolled his left ankle in Friday’s preseason finale against the Celtics, while Barlow is dealing with back soreness. 76ers head coach Nick Nurse said after Friday’s game that Wade’s ankle injury wasn’t a major concern, which could bode well for his availability Tuesday night. Neither Wade nor Barlow is in a position to be players who absolutely need to be rostered in fantasy leagues. However, Philadelphia’s injury-riddled frontcourt frees up minutes at the forward spots. 
 Jabari Walker 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #33 
 Jabari Walker with 13 points (4-of-8 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), four rebounds, two steals in 19 minutes against the Celtics. 
 Jabari Walker has proven that he can play in an NBA rotation and he should have a role on this Philadelphia team. While Dean Wade will likely start when there’s injuries, Walker will still be important in deeper leagues as a consistent producer that will likely get a bump when there are injuries. 
 Jabari Walker 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #33 
 Jabari Walker finished Monday’s exhibition against the Knicks with 11 points (4-of-9 FGs), 11 rebounds, one assist, one steal, one block and three three-pointers. 
 Walker’s contract for the upcoming season isn’t fully guaranteed until January 10, so he still has work to do. He looked sharp in Monday’s preseason opener, shooting 3-of-5 from beyond the arc and showing more confidence in his shot than last season. Walker’s role may also grow in importance because of injuries to Philadelphia’s other rotation bigs. Adem Bona (foot) is recovering from a sprain, while Ariel Hukporti suffered a lower-right-leg injury in the first half of Monday’s game. Given starting center Joel Embiid’s injury history, Walker is someone to watch with Bona and Hukporti sidelined. 
 Ariel Hukporti 
 PHI 
 Center 
 #55 
 VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Dean Wade and Ariel Hukporti will start Monday’s exhibition against the Knicks. 
 The 76ers will open their preseason without multiple key players, including Tyrese Maxey, LeBron James and Joel Embiid. With those expected starters unavailable, KCP, Wade and Hukporti will start. The latter may be the one to watch, as he’ll be competing with the currently injured Adem Bona for the right to back up Embiid. There isn’t much to gain from drafting Hukporti in most leagues, but Embiid’s injury history makes it possible that the former Knick will be a relevant streamer at some point during the regular season. 
 Johni Broome 
 PHI 
 Forward 
 #22 
 NBA insider Jake Fischer reports that the 76ers have been seeking “trade avenues” to move on from Johni Broome. 
 Philadelphia’s reported interest in moving on from Broome has more to do with the pending signing of Kentavious Caldwell-Pope than anything else. Just as the team needed to waive Dalen Terry to have the roster spot needed to make the LeBron James signing official, another roster spot is needed to add KCP. Broome, who was limited to 11 NBA appearances last season and missed time with a knee injury, played well during Summer League. Still, the 76ers have Adem Bona and Ariel Hukporti to absorb minutes behind starting center Joel Embiid. In the right situation, Broome could have some streaming value throughout the season. According to Fischer, waiving Jabari Walker is another possibility, but the 76ers hope to hold onto him. 
 Dean Wade 
 CLE 
 Forward-Center 
 #32 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the 76ers have agreed to sign Dean Wade. 
 Wade was a solid contributor for the Cavaliers last season, a perimeter threat who could also defend at the forward spot. He spent all seven of his NBA seasons with Cleveland but will now depart to Philadelphia and likely play a similar role. Wade averaged 5.8 points and 4.2 rebounds on 43.9/36.2/71.1 shooting splits last season.

 Kyrie Irving had 15 points (6-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal and one three-pointer against the Rockets on Wednesday. 
 Irving was limited to just 23 minutes against the Rockets Wednesday as he was returning from injury. The 34-year-old point guard missed all of last season with a torn ACL and a calf strain. Irving still scored 15 points on nine attempts in those 23 minutes. Expect his minutes and production to increase as the Mavericks ease him into the beginning of the regular season.

 Cooper Flagg had 32 points (10-of-17 FGs, 11-of-13 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, three steals, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s game against the Rockets. 
 Flagg filled up the stat sheet and dropped 32 points in the Mavericks season opener. There’s not much more you could ask from the 19-year-old, which shows how much of an uphill battle it might be for Dallas this year as the Mavericks lost to the Rockets by 18. Flagg and the Mavericks have two more games this week with a back-to-back against the Pacers and Spurs on Friday and Saturday.

 Oso Ighodaro (hip) will not return to Wednesday’s game against the Trail Blazers. 
 Ighodaro took a hit to his right hip during the second quarter of Wednesday’s game. Although he initially tried to play through the injury, the 7-footer was subbed out with just over a minute left in the half. Ighodaro didn’t return to the bench for the third quarter, and he’s done for the night. Khaman Maluach, who started Wednesday’s game, should play more minutes while Duop Reath slides into the back end of the rotation.

 Şengün didn’t record any blocks or steals in this one, but he was +23 in 29 minutes as the Rockets won by 18. The 24-year-old center had a double-double with 23 points and 10 rebounds. He also made both of his three-point attempts. After a what was considered a down-year for him last year, Şengün got off to a good start this season.

 Kevin Durant had 30 points (10-of-16 FGs, 8-of-11 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in the Rockerts’ 128-110 victory over the Mavericks on Wednesday. 
 Durant started his 19th season in the NBA off with an excellent performance. The 38-year-old forward dropped 30 points on 16 attempts as the Rockets won going away over the Mavericks. Durant played 37 minutes after averaging 36.3 minutes last season. While the Rockets’ top brass has talked about managing his minutes, Durant wasn’t held back at all in the season opener.

 Davion Mitchell produced 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 10 assists, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 The good news for fantasy managers was that Mitchell recorded a double-double, which included a game-high 10 assists. However, for category-league managers, the six turnovers hurt. Mitchell logged 33 minutes in Wednesday’s opener, with Pelle Larsson (two points, three rebounds, four assists, one steal and one block) taking on the playmaking responsibilities when “Off Night” was on the bench. Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo can also initiate the offense, and they’ll likely need to because Miami lacks depth at point guard. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Klay Thompson notched 10 points (3-of-6 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), one rebound and three three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 After making two of his three three-point attempts and scoring six points in the first quarter, Thompson did not provide much value in his official Heat debut. While starting was a positive for the veteran guard, he played just 16 minutes. Meanwhile, Tim Hardaway Jr. (three points, four rebounds, one assist, one steal and one three-pointer) logged 18 minutes off the bench. Outside of deep leagues where you need three-pointers, you gain little by rostering Thompson.

 Dejounte Murray had 23 points (9-of-18 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, seven assists, two steals, three blocks and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s game against the Pacers. 
 Murray filled up the stat sheet in the loss to the Pacers Wednesday. The 30-year-old point guard was excellent and showed he could be in for a bounce back season after playing just 45 games over the past two seasons combined. Murray was also playing through a bruised toe that he suffered during the preseason.

 Bam Adebayo posted 15 points (6-of-12 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), seven rebounds, four assists, three steals and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 After scoring six points on 3-of-9 shooting in the first half, Adebayo scored nine in the third quarter. Unfortunately for fantasy managers, the Heat center went scoreless in the fourth, attempting just one shot. The on-court chemistry between Adebayo and Giannis Antetokounmpo needs work, which isn’t a surprise. But at times, Bam looked like little more than a bystander on offense, and that can’t happen.

 Giannis Antetokounmpo tallied 35 points (13-of-19 FGs, 9-of-14 FTs), six rebounds, one assist and one steal in Wednesday’s loss to the Timberwolves.
 Giannis came out hot in his official Heat debut, scoring 14 points in the first quarter. He went into the halftime break with 21, but no other Heat player scored more than seven. Antetokounmpo finished with a solid stat line, but fantasy managers may have hoped for more on the defensive end. The Heat host the Pistons Friday in the first of two games in as many nights before visiting Charlotte on Saturday.
